subject: [PATCH] mm, swap: revalidate populated clusters before scanning

reviews.author: Youngjun Park
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the relocated cluster check is missing a table allocation check, and suggested adding it to prevent NULL pointer dereferences.

Reviewer noted that publishing the table after acquiring the cluster lock, as suggested by Kemeng, is also a correct approach to prevent the issue described in the linked email and requested further consideration of this alternative solution.
reviews.raw_body:
Hello Nhat.

Good catch!

---

If this patch is applied as bloew, does it prevent the issue described here?

https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20260720071342.50742-2-shikemeng@huaweicloud.com/
(This patch publishes cluster table after lock acquired.)

This patch is chagned the way I suggested during review... :(

As you pointed out, another context can free the table 
without alloc context knwoing this situation.  
I missed this situation.

IMHO, Publishing the table only after reacquiring the cluster lock, as Kemeng
suggested, and rejecting an unusable cluster under the lock as in this
patch both look correct to me!

Reviewed-by: Youngjun Park <youngjun.park@lge.com>

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary:
Author expressed surprise and confusion about the status of their patch series, implying they were not aware it was still being reviewed.

Author acknowledges that swap_cluster_alloc_table() does not hold nor acquire cluster's lock, making it vulnerable to table freeing between publishing and subsequent lock acquisition. Author suggests two possible approaches to address this issue: either lock the cluster before publishing the table or enforce metadata lifetime through a reference count.
reviews.raw_body:
Ah I missed that patch series and your review! What happened to it?
Did we just never land it?

Looks like we are still doing neither Keming's approach (table
copying) nor your approach (publishing at the end of
swap_cluster_alloc_table()).

---

Yeah I feel like it's still not safe with your approach...
swap_cluster_alloc_table() does not hold nor acquire cluster's lock.
Between its publishing of the table and the subsequent lock
acquisition in its caller (swap_cluster_populate()), someone can still
come in and free the table.

It's tricky. We do not have an explicit contract for the metadata's
lifetime, so it's a bit of reading the tea leaves for me...

I think this is the last gap, and it's rare enough, so this simple
check should suffice to cover the edgiest of the edge cases :) But who
knows :) If bugs re-surfaced again, I think we can spend a bit more
time ironcladding the lifetime of clusters/tables:

1. Allocate outside of lock context, but make swap_cluster_populate()
lock the cluster, check cluster's status, and only then publish the
table (and return with the cluster locked). Basically Keming's
approach.

2. Carefully enforce metadata's lifetime. Perhaps we can add a refcnt?
In addition to occupied slots holding cluster's refcnt, we can allow
for temporary holders. As long as we can acquire a refcnt, we know for
sure the metadata is not freed under us. This is my approach for the
old vswap patch series, but it's tricky, especially with caching in
the picture.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that another patch already implements the suggested approach, but still thinks their original patch is necessary and suggests it might be a small fix or an alternative to Kemeng's proposal.
sentiment_signals: still thinks own patch is necessary
reviews.raw_body:
Ah nope, I saw that Kemeng implemented your approach:

https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20260907091356.53026-2-shikemeng@huaweicloud.com/

My bad! But yeah I think we still need this small fix (or Kemeng's
original proposal?), unless I missed something...?

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary:
Author inquires about additional callsites where the issue might occur, suggesting uncertainty about the scope of the problem.

Author is considering the reviewer's suggestion to add a lock, but needs more time to think about it and hasn't committed to making any changes yet.
reviews.raw_body:
Do we have another callsite? There's a callsite in setup code, but I
assume that's safe...?

But at this point, who knows any more. The caching only stores a
swapfile struct, and an offset. I wonder if there is a potential race
between swapoff-then-re-swapon and cached allocation? That'd be pretty
wild.

---

Hmm so a bitlock?

Lemme think about it a bit.

2026-10-20.patch_summary: This patch revalidates populated clusters before scanning to prevent dereferencing a NULL table. It checks if the cluster's table is allocated and relocates it only when its table is present. This fix addresses an issue where a cached allocator can use and empty a cluster's table before the populating allocator reacquires the lock, leading to a NULL pointer dereference during scanning.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the swapoff path needs to drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), but couldn't reproduce the issue and will report back if they manage to do so.
reviews.raw_body:
I'm revisiting the lifecycle of clusters, because vswap introduced
dynamic (i.e run-time freeing) behavior to it. For the most part it
looks good (both physical and virtual side), but this look racy to me.
I don't see how it can be safe. Once you drop the lock, all bets are
off...

But at the same time, I have not been able to reproduce it (yet). Will
report here if I manage to.

(Side note: my vswap code is actually safe in this scenario. CPU0
allocates a new cluster entirely, and lock it before publishing it. So
even if the cluster index is cached in CPU1, this race cannot happen).

It checks if the cluster's table is allocated and relocates it only when its table is present. This fix addresses an issue where a cached allocator can use and empty a cluster's table before the populating allocator reacquires the lock, leading to a NULL pointer dereference during scanning.

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kairui Song noted that the patch does not fully address the issue of calling swap_cluster_alloc_table() without holding the ci lock, and suggested adding a 'bool locked' parameter to this function to ensure it locks the ci before assigning tables. This change would also prevent misuse as reported by Kemeng earlier.
reviews.raw_body:
Nice catch!

I think the real problem is that it turns out calling
swap_cluster_alloc_table() without holding ci lock is bad idea... I
think this patch still leaves some other call site too?

We may instead add a "bool locked" to swap_cluster_alloc_table, and
let it lock the ci first before it does any assign (not the alloc) if
the allocation context is not locked. That is, keep the
sleep-allocated tables private until swap_cluster_populate()
reacquires local/global/ci, then install them under ci->lock,
something like pre-cdd77f84d966, always assign it atomically.

That should also cover the problem reported by Kemeng a few weeks
earlier too, and prevent further misuse. My Bad on that change :P

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kairui Song expressed uncertainty about the first patch being perfect and mentioned that they had previously acknowledged part of it, but were waiting for an update from Kemeng due to their email bouncing back.
reviews.raw_body:
Right I remember that, I acked part of that and was waiting the update

Kemeng's mail at "shikemeng@huaweicloud.com" is now bouncing back...
I'm not sure if Kemeng still plans to update that.

2026-10-21.patch_summary: This patch revalidates populated clusters before scanning to prevent dereferencing a NULL table. It checks if the cluster's table is allocated and relocates it only when its table is present. This fix addresses an issue where a cached allocator can use and empty a cluster's table before the populating allocator reacquires the lock, leading to a NULL pointer dereference during scanning.
